status: approved requirements snapshot; source harness only, no terminal acceptance
epicDescription:
### Objective

SceneWorks provides optional, predictor-driven Veda block-sparse MiniMax-H3 DiT attention through its native MLX and Candle/CUDA engines and normal product request path. T2VA, FL2VA and R2VA, every shipped H3 quant tier, Turbo and style LoRAs, all existing input carriers, and the complete frozen upstream control surface remain supported. Off preserves the current dense result. On executes the selected sparse kernel when supported and reports any dense fallback clearly. Managed predictor integrity, bounded memory admission, observed execution status, and Michael-reviewed fixed-seed dense/sparse quality evidence are part of delivery.

### Requirements

**E1 — Opt-in, default off.** Veda is disabled unless explicitly selected. With Veda off, a seeded render is bit-identical to the pre-feature dense path on both MLX and Candle/CUDA, using identical model artifacts, quant tier, adapters, conditioning, seed, schedule and geometry. Sparse initialization, predictor loading and workspace allocation must not run in the off path. Existing saved requests without Veda settings retain their behavior.

**E2 — Same frozen selection everywhere.** Tiling, complete embedded tile-plan table, pooled-QK scorer and selection reproduce `veda-sparse/Veda-on-ComfyUI@60bfae688897dc41bc8685ca9f3130d7ed8f3b0c`. The selected block masks are backend-independent and exactly match frozen upstream fixtures on identical inputs. Preserve 128-token tile ordering, valid-row prefixes and padding masks; all twelve 50-layer × 56-head plans; nearest log-aspect including transpose, then nearest temporal length, then least-padding plan choice; masked mean/max/min TripPool; FP8 E4M3FN × per-head scale decoded through BF16 projection storage before FP32 projection/logit arithmetic; residual mean addition and division by sqrt(head dimension); dense global queries/keys; separate reference/generated column budgets; equal-kernel-cost ratio `keep_ratio × ceil(real_tokens/128)^2 / column_tiles`; Bresenham fractional allocation; forced diagonal consuming budget; and exclusion of empty keys. Fixtures include partial tiles, transposed/nearest plans, separate reference blocks, near ties and ties. Attention-output tolerance cannot substitute for exact selected-mask parity.

**E3 — Full native surface.** T2VA, FL2VA and R2VA run through MLX and Candle/CUDA across every shipped H3 quant tier, including q4, q8 and bf16. Turbo and style LoRAs continue to stack through the existing runtime adapter mechanism. First/last images, R2VA image references, reference clips with their available soundtracks, standalone audio references, mixed reference carriers and supported batch shapes retain their existing semantics. A mode/device/dtype/kernel/layout that cannot execute sparse uses dense attention with a visible reason. No backend, tier, adapter regime, product canvas or supported mode is silently removed because a prototype is slow or unavailable. Backend implementation choices follow measured S0 evidence; no MLX scope reduction is authorized.

**E4 — Kernel self-test.** Each selected sparse kernel passes an on-device check before first use against the same mask's dense reference, with a declared tolerance owned by that kernel. The check includes reference, generated, global and partial/padded rows and asserts the output is not unmasked dense attention. A failed self-test yields dense attention and a visible reason. There is one declared sparse kernel route per supported device path, with no silent sparse-kernel fallback chain. Cache validity is tied to the applicable device/kernel identity rather than an unrelated earlier test.

**E5 — Complete user controls.** Expose independent generated sparsity and reference sparsity, each accepting a sparsity percentage or an absolute positive key-tile count; full-attention layer lists; and full-attention sampling-step lists. Lists are zero-based and validated against the applicable layer/step domain. The actual step index reaches every attention call, including both native backends. The frozen defaults are 90% video sparsity with empty dense layer/step lists when enabled; do not silently substitute upstream 0.3.1's newer fixed-32 default. Explicit reference 0% sparsity keeps its keys dense. Product persistence, request validation, raw settings and replay preserve the selected settings, and incompatible-model or malformed inputs are refused at the appropriate API/worker boundary.

**E6 — Visible observed status.** Job results and telemetry identify the effective kernel, matched tile plan, nearest trained size when out of distribution, actual percentage of full attention computed, and any dense-fallback reasons. Requested settings remain separate from observed execution. Deliberate dense layers/steps and mandatory global attention contribute correctly to the denominator; requested 90% video sparsity must not be presented as the actual total-attention reduction. Observed facts come from inference after generation, rather than from worker settings assembled before generation. Studio results/replay expose these facts without silently implying that an enabled request ran sparse.

**E7 — Managed exact predictor.** Both H3 catalog entries provision the predictor through the existing managed co-requisite download path. Frozen predictor: repository `Veda-Sparse/Minimax-H3-T2VA-Veda-8NFE-600Step-Preview`, revision `9a1fd3a41b4a754a7886e64e82edbddf599fd1bd`, file `minimax_h3_t2va_veda_8nfe_600step_preview_fp8.safetensors`, 275,415,648 bytes, SHA256 `2a8d8845c5342756a2781e8e69563940e4bb573c9a40ebb534915ff8fd76573a`. The exact digest travels through schema, authoritative catalog payload, queued download, downloader/cache reuse and load-time integrity validation. A local cached file is not accepted solely because its filename or size matches. No ad-hoc fetch, unpinned main resolution, process-global predictor path or inference-side network fallback is allowed. Missing/corrupt predictor gives a visible dense fallback with a repair/install reason; off remains usable. A soft co-requisite and cache-only optional component staging prevent predictor absence from making the dense model unavailable. No newly discovered R2VA predictor is selected implicitly.

**E8 — Correct sparse memory admission.** Sparse workspace is bounded by the actual problem, not expanded to consume free memory. Account for predictor host and device residency, pooled/scorer/selection intermediates, mask/index arrays, tile-order and gathered QKV copies, retained/final outputs, and kernel scratch in H3 memory estimation and admission on both backends. Bounds include any minimum batch exceeding an allowance; an inner score budget does not bound a gather already allocated. MLX batching combines heads sharing a tile shape and multiple independent query tiles, then materializes each bounded output chunk before allocating the next. Global query rows stay separate from sparse video batches. Sparse requests do not borrow dense-only memory evidence, and fallback is priced safely. Existing measured evidence remains useful; source/pin currency is advisory and does not authorize remeasurement per story or resurrect dismantled gates.

**E9 — Full quality evidence.** Every shipped configuration in the mode × published recipe steps × product-size-bucket matrix receives a fixed-seed sparse/dense A/B with PSNR and a side-by-side reviewed by Michael. Include T2VA, first-image/last-image/both-image FL2VA, multimodal R2VA, all H3 tiers and both native backends, base 50-step and all published 4-/8-step Turbo recipes, and compatible Turbo-plus-style adapter stacks. The nine published canvases are `1536x672`, `672x1536`, `1344x768`, `768x1344`, `1024x768`, `768x1024`, `768x768`, `576x320`, `320x576`; each is a matrix bucket, not a reason to collapse distinct geometry to a trained example. Out-of-distribution 4-step, 50-step, R2VA and product-size configurations are explicit rows. A/B holds artifacts, input carriers, prompts, adapter weights, schedule, seed and geometry constant. PSNR is measured on decoded aligned output and retained with timing/peak-memory facts; synchronized audio is retained for review and compared separately. No PSNR threshold or visual-quality approval is invented. Michael's review is the quality acceptance decision. Local fixtures, random-mask timing and upstream samples do not constitute generated-media acceptance.

### Epic acceptance

The single terminal story proves the integrated contract once:

1. Frozen upstream exact selected-mask fixtures pass on both backends, and omitted/off Veda settings preserve seeded dense identity. The final native request/loader path, not a standalone toy selection function, reaches this proof.
2. Every kernel's on-device sparse-reference and not-dense tests pass; forced missing-predictor, corrupt-predictor, unsupported-kernel and failed-self-test cases visibly execute the documented dense fallback. Full-attention layer/step controls and independent reference/generated budgets have their expected effects.
3. The complete E9 case manifest drives native real-weight renders on both backends. Each cell retains request/artifact/driver/seed identity, active tier/adapters, effective status, step/whole-job time, peak host/device memory, PSNR, audio comparison and side-by-side media with Michael's review disposition. Failure/OOM/fallback cells are explicit outcomes to resolve, not silently skipped matrix entries. Performance is compared with SceneWorks' own current dense engines.
4. Sparse predictor/workspace bytes agree with the admitted workload and observed peaks within the documented bound. Problem-size/OOD/long-duration and reference-heavy cases exercise admission; a free-memory-dependent work buffer cannot masquerade as a problem bound.
5. Both repositories' integration heads and required/affected CI lanes are green. One feature-end adversarial review, limited to at most three review/fix cycles, completes. Inference lands in its `main` first; SceneWorks takes exactly one final pin to the verified inference `main` commit, refreshes required pin-derived artifacts using current procedures, completes the terminal acceptance campaign, then merges its completed feature to `main`. Final ref ancestry, pin, status checks, story/epic association and tracker state are read back. No release/promotion is implied.

**Terminal case manifest.** Catalog source is authoritative and must be re-read before the campaign. Current defaults: 24 fps, 1344x768, 124 frames (5.1667 s), base 50 NFE. Frame lattice is 17n+5; published durations span 124–345 frames. Published accelerator recipes, all in the `minimax-h3` family:

| Adapter regime | NFE | Video shift | Audio shift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Base, Turbo off | 50 | 12 | 3 |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_4step_768p` | 4 | 6 | 3 |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_8step` | 8 | 12 | 3 |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_4step_v01` | 4 | 12 | 3 |
| `minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step` | 4 | 12 | 3 |

Cross these published regimes with every E9 mode, all nine canvas buckets, both backends and all shipped tiers, plus compatible style-adapter coverage. Derive actual adapter compatibility from the catalog/runtime contract; do not infer that an adapter's name restricts its family-wide advertised eligibility. Explicit user step overrides continue to work; 4 and 50 NFE stay explicit OOD proof points even though the predictor was trained under Turbo 8 NFE. Duration coverage additionally includes short/default 124 frames, middle 243 frames, long 345 frames, and a nearest-plan nonexact temporal point such as 141 frames, with case identities retained. All published duration choices and input caps have source-backed boundary checks. Matrix execution may be batched/resumed, but required cells are never dropped to meet a resource/time estimate.

**S0 evidence and pending decisions.** Frozen source and native source inspection are complete. Correctly batched MLX gather+SDPA S0 was measured on Apple M5 Max with 128 GiB unified memory from clean inference `fd146a276545b2a8168939ec34e3862911b425fe`, binary SHA256 `c78f899a8ae95c61fe20786cc10e646eb7c9d2c302ae0408ec8ed94ff419792e`. Same random BF16 QKV/key plan, warmup plus three measured runs:

| Canvas | Tokens | Dense layer median | Sparse layer median | Dense/sparse | Dense peak | Sparse peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 576x320 | 7,586 | 0.038734 s | 0.064262 s | 0.603x | 435,027,968 B | 689,553,408 B |
| 1344x768 | 38,222 | 2.522392 s | 0.727180 s | 3.469x | 2,191,851,520 B | 2,739,814,400 B |

The small BF16 masked-reference oracle error was 0.0 against a declared prototype tolerance 0.025, with not-dense and padding assertions. Device gathers/index/mask/SDPA/concatenation/evaluation are timed; host random-plan preparation and learned predictor scoring are excluded. This establishes native batching feasibility, not frozen predictor parity or generated-media speed/quality. Sparse peaks are higher and must be priced. The earlier head-by-query-tile evaluation loop is not a fair upstream batching comparison.

Actual q4 DiT profiling from source `e47218ea1505fd07bf53f6f2b02ca9f3c3bc94d4`, binary `9c17b32378e666c46a3baacb39afa015e28215ffb4a35f46a554ce7f83bce568`, exercised 50 attention calls in one measured forward: profiled attention share was 22.508% at 576x320 and 61.197% at 1344x768. Synchronization perturbed the full forward by -2.710% and +9.339%, respectively. Do not combine these instrumented shares with the random-layer ratio to claim full-render speedup.

Verified evidence resides at `/Users/michael/Documents/Codex/2026-10-10/epic-25140/s0-results.md` and `verified-s0-summary.json`, with exact source/binary/exit receipts and JSONL logs. **PENDING S0 APPENDIX: native direct sparse Metal comparison and CUDA numerical/timing/real-DiT evidence.** The coordinator will attach verified final receipts/conclusions before presenting a final implementation recommendation. Pending evidence does not remove either backend or any product mode. Choose the declared MLX/CUDA kernel implementations from fair native comparisons; preserve the requirement surface regardless of a slower small-canvas result.

Upstream-reported numbers are separate historical evidence: Veda-on-ComfyUI reported RTX 5070 8-NFE T2VA attention 4.41 s/step against ComfyUI default 31.1 s and SageAttention 15.2 s; its M3 Pro gather result 3.52 s was compared with PyTorch MPS SDPA 9.29 s. None is a SceneWorks native acceptance result. The frozen checkpoint has twelve plans, while training used T2VA conditioning on the FL2VA backbone under Turbo 8 NFE. Transfer claims for arbitrary modalities/steps/adapters require the E9 native quality campaign.

### Slice plan

Use mirrored `feature/sc-25140-minimax-h3-veda` integration branches, with story branches targeting the owning feature branch. SceneWorks source baseline for this proposal is `bedcd85a969b39c8357c971ea93f185b46d7c22b`; current inference pin is `25bd55cdb6a56c78b07584a12150c9f5d46be439`. Re-query refs, resource ownership, story applicability and live CI protections before execution.

1. **S1 — Native MLX H3 predictor-driven walking path:** one genuine native generation path establishes request/component/control/report contracts and default-off behavior, locally proven with bounded fixtures/device smoke.
2. **S2 — Complete frozen selector, plans and reference tiling:** fills the backend-independent numerical/selection surface and exact fixtures; depends on S1.
3. **S3 — Native CUDA sparse kernel and self-test:** one declared native kernel executes selected blocks with the frozen arithmetic and explicit failure behavior; depends on S1.
4. **S4 — Full native H3 modes, tiers, adapters and attention controls:** carries all existing generation/conditioning/regime choices and step/layer controls through both engines; depends on S1.
5. **S5 — Managed predictor exact digest and offline component staging:** catalog-to-download-to-load integrity with repairable missing/corrupt fallback; depends on S1.
6. **S6 — SceneWorks opt-in controls and native request/replay plumbing:** exposes the complete control surface through product/API/worker and preserves Turbo/style/tier routing; depends on S4 and S5.
7. **S7 — Observed sparse outcome results and telemetry:** records actual kernel/plan/attention/fallback facts and exposes them in results; depends on S1.
8. **S8 — Problem-bounded sparse residency and admission:** prices complete predictor/workspace lifetimes and preserves conservative fallback admission; depends on S1.
9. **S9 — Terminal acceptance, review and paired-main integration:** converges S1–S8, owns the full real-weight campaign, Michael review, final review, single pin and tracker readback; depends on S2–S8.

S2/S3/S4/S5/S7/S8 are independent wideners after S1; they share interfaces and reconcile overlapping changes through their feature branches. S4's local tests exercise typed routes and explicit unavailable-kernel behavior; S2/S3 supply complete kernels/selection before terminal acceptance. Ordinary story AC do not own the full real-weight matrix. Review is consolidated at terminal acceptance, at most three review/fix cycles, under the coordinator's current execution instructions.

### Out of scope

Training new predictors, choosing the newer released R2VA predictor without a separate approved change, extending Veda to unrelated model families, TMA/cluster CUDA variants, release publication or feature promotion into `release/next`, and ad-hoc weight fetching are outside this epic. None of these boundaries excludes existing H3 modes, tiers, LoRAs, controls, native backends or approved acceptance requirements. Reuse applicable fused-kernel work from epic 23989 only when source-ready; do not make a dependency on the entire unrelated epic. Disabled verification gates remain disabled.

stories.description:

Include T2VA, first-image/last-image/both-image FL2VA, multimodal R2VA, all H3 tiers and both native backends, base 50-step and all published 4-/8-step Turbo recipes, and compatible Turbo-plus-style adapter stacks. The nine published canvases are `1536x672`, `672x1536`, `1344x768`, `768x1344`, `1024x768`, `768x1024`, `768x768`, `576x320`, `320x576`; each is a matrix bucket, not a reason to collapse distinct geometry to a trained example. Out-of-distribution 4-step, 50-step, R2VA and product-size configurations are explicit rows. A/B holds artifacts, input carriers, prompts, adapter weights, schedule, seed and geometry constant. PSNR is measured on decoded aligned output and retained with timing/peak-memory facts; synchronized audio is retained for review and compared separately. No PSNR threshold or visual-quality approval is invented. Michael's review is the quality acceptance decision. Local fixtures, random-mask timing and upstream samples do not constitute generated-media acceptance.
literalAuthority.terminal_case_manifest:
**Terminal case manifest.** Catalog source is authoritative and must be re-read before the campaign. Current defaults: 24 fps, 1344x768, 124 frames (5.1667 s), base 50 NFE. Frame lattice is 17n+5; published durations span 124–345 frames. Published accelerator recipes, all in the `minimax-h3` family:

| Adapter regime | NFE | Video shift | Audio shift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Base, Turbo off | 50 | 12 | 3 |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_4step_768p` | 4 | 6 | 3 |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_8step` | 8 | 12 | 3 |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_4step_v01` | 4 | 12 | 3 |
| `minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step` | 4 | 12 | 3 |

Cross these published regimes with every E9 mode, all nine canvas buckets, both backends and all shipped tiers, plus compatible style-adapter coverage. Derive actual adapter compatibility from the catalog/runtime contract; do not infer that an adapter's name restricts its family-wide advertised eligibility. Explicit user step overrides continue to work; 4 and 50 NFE stay explicit OOD proof points even though the predictor was trained under Turbo 8 NFE. Duration coverage additionally includes short/default 124 frames, middle 243 frames, long 345 frames, and a nearest-plan nonexact temporal point such as 141 frames, with case identities retained. All published duration choices and input caps have source-backed boundary checks. Matrix execution may be batched/resumed, but required cells are never dropped to meet a resource/time estimate.

modelIds_schema.description: The exact model ids this adapter may attach to (sc-19563). OPTIONAL, and absent means family gating alone — so this never tightens an existing entry. When present, validate_lora_specs_for_model refuses the LoRA on any model id outside this list, EVEN WITHIN THE SAME FAMILY. That is the case `family` cannot express: MiniMax-H3 publishes `minimax_h3` (t2va/fl2va) and `minimax_h3_ref` (ref2va) as one DiT architecture with one geometry, so both declare `family: minimax-h3` and both accept `minimax-h3` LoRAs — yet lightx2v distils the fl2v and ref2v turbo adapters for one partition each. Cross-selecting is shape-valid and folds cleanly, which is what made it a quality mismatch rather than a failure. Deliberately a LIST, not the singular `baseModel` the Wan gate reads: `baseModel` is a value a trained or imported adapter RECORDS about itself, while this is a catalog author DECLARING which partitions an adapter is for, and one adapter can legitimately serve several.
